documents: Two forms of ID (one must be a passport), proof of foreign address, proof of income and a bank reference; branch visit required.
min_deposit_fees: Opening deposit required but amount not published for non-residents.
banks: First Citizens Bank (publishes non-resident requirements); Republic Bank (non-resident category, branch only).
restrictions: Online onboarding (RepublicOnboard) is for nationals; USD/foreign-currency availability is constrained by chronic FX shortages; strict AML/KYC and CRS/FATCA reporting.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for holding/paying in USD; TT dollar local details not offered by major fintechs.

documents: Passport, Mexican residence card (temporal/permanente) for most banks, proof of address under 3 months old, tax ID (RFC or foreign TIN); tourists on an FMM generally refused.
min_deposit_fees: Not published for non-residents; some banks impose minimum balances and withdrawal limits on non-resident accounts.
banks: Some branches of major banks (e.g. BBVA México, Banamex, Banorte) open accounts case-by-case; most require residency.
restrictions: Almost all banks require residency; non-resident accounts often restricted (card-only, transfer limits); USD accounts limited to border-zone residents; CRS/FATCA reporting.
alternatives: Wise (MXN transfers), Revolut; digital banks offering card-only wallets without residency.

documents: Venezuelan cédula de identidad and RIF tax ID, local proof of address, proof of income and personal/bank references; in-branch processing.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: None known for non-residents; Banco de Venezuela, Banco Mercantil and BNC require local cédula/RIF and Venezuelan address.
restrictions: US OFAC and other sanctions on the government and state banks, severe correspondent-banking de-risking, hyperinflation history and exchange controls; USD access largely via cash or Zelle-type informal channels.
alternatives: Foreigners typically use home-country accounts with cash USD, Zinli/Binance P2P or employer-managed accounts; no mainstream fintech local details.

documents: Passport, Argentine tax ID (CUIT/CUIL; CUIT replaced CDI for foreigners from March 2026), local proof of address; DNI needed for full product range and online banking.
min_deposit_fees: Basic accounts (caja de ahorro / cuenta para migrantes at public banks) are free; other fees not published for non-residents.
banks: Banco de la Nación Argentina and other public banks (mandated basic accounts); private banks case-by-case.
restrictions: Many branches refuse passport-only applicants; non-residents face tighter product limits; FX rules eased from April 2025 but still evolving; FATCA/CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise, Western Union, crypto/USDT apps commonly used; local wallets such as Mercado Pago generally require DNI.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign residential address (within 3 months), tax residency/TIN declaration, sometimes source-of-funds or reference; Singapore pass needed for digital (Singpass) opening.
min_deposit_fees: Non-resident accounts often need higher deposits (roughly up to S$5,000 or more at priority tiers); e.g. DBS Multiplier S$3,000 average balance or S$5 monthly fee.
banks: DBS, OCBC, UOB, Citibank Singapore, Standard Chartered, HSBC Singapore (case-by-case, often via priority/wealth tiers).
restrictions: Strict MAS AML/KYC; many retail products require a pass or local address; non-residents frequently asked to visit a branch in person; CRS/FATCA reporting.
alternatives: Wise and Revolut provide SGD local account details; YouTrip and other wallets for spending.

documents: Passport with valid entry/employment/student/dependent pass and local proof of address (Brunei licence, utility bill or employer letter) for standard accounts.
min_deposit_fees: Baiduri savings account minimum opening deposit BND 100; non-resident terms not published.
banks: Baiduri Bank and BIBD (resident-focused; non-resident case-by-case); Standard Chartered Brunei.
restrictions: No exchange controls and non-resident accounts permitted by law, but banks generally want a local pass; US persons face hurdles due to no FATCA IGA.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for transfers; BND is pegged 1:1 to SGD so Singapore accounts are a practical substitute.

documents: Passport and visa/permit documentation, proof of address, source of funds and references; in-branch identification.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: ANZ Solomon Islands, BSP Solomon Islands, Bank of South Pacific; non-resident personal accounts case-by-case.
restrictions: Central Bank of Solomon Islands exchange controls; foreign-currency accounts need central bank approval; withholding tax on non-resident interest; strict PEP rules.
alternatives: Wise/Revolut from Australia for transfers; mobile money services limited.

documents: Passport (with notarised Azerbaijani translation if needed); some banks also request local registration, residence permit or tax ID.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: Kapital Bank (Birbank) and ABB reportedly open accounts for non-residents with passport at a branch; policies vary.
restrictions: Central Bank currency regulations allow non-resident accounts in AZN and FX, but banks apply own residence-permit rules; remote onboarding requires ASAN Imza e-signature; CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise and Revolut for transfers; few local fintechs open to non-residents.

documents: Passport with valid visa or residence card, accommodation certificate, proof of earnings (Chad-specific Ecobank requirement), notarised copies for non-residents.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: Ecobank Tchad (non-resident accounts subject to local regulation, branch visit expected); no bank known to routinely open for non-residents.
restrictions: CEMAC/BEAC foreign-exchange regulation tightly controls foreign-currency and non-resident accounts; XAF-to-FX conversions need justification; high AML scrutiny and de-risking.
alternatives: Mobile money (Airtel Money, Moov Money) requires local SIM/ID; foreigners generally rely on home-country accounts and remittance services.

documents: Passport, visa or residence/work permit (bank-dependent), proof of address, two photos, TRA TIN (non-residents can apply online), opening deposit.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: CRDB Bank, NMB Bank, Stanbic, Standard Chartered Tanzania (permit usually requested; case-by-case for non-residents).
restrictions: Foreign Exchange Regulations 2022 allow residents and non-residents to hold FX accounts locally; many banks still demand a permit; strict KYC.
alternatives: Mobile money (M-Pesa, Tigo Pesa/Mixx, Airtel Money) needs local SIM registered with NIDA or passport; Wise transfers into TZS.

documents: Passport with visa endorsement, proof of foreign address, source of funds; in-person FICA verification or notarised documents couriered to the branch.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: FNB Namibia (non-resident foreign currency accounts), Bank Windhoek (non-resident accounts with notarised remote route reported).
restrictions: Common Monetary Area exchange controls administered by Bank of Namibia; non-resident accounts flagged and FX flows reported; FIA AML/KYC requirements.
alternatives: Wise transfers to NAD; South African bank non-resident accounts usable within the CMA.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign home address, proof of income/source of funds, tax ID (TIN) declaration; traditional banks often want a Meldebescheinigung; notarised copies if opening remotely.
min_deposit_fees: Not published for non-residents; standard current accounts typically cost a few EUR per month.
banks: Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, Sparkassen case-by-case in branch; online banks N26 and bunq require a German/EEA address.
restrictions: Basic payment account right (Basiskonto) covers persons legally resident in the EU, not non-EU non-residents; strict GwG KYC; CRS/FATCA reporting.
alternatives: Wise and Revolut offer EUR IBANs to Australian residents; N26/bunq need EEA residence.

documents: Passport plus second ID, proof of home-country address, tax residence certificate/TIN, sometimes residence permit; translations may be required.
min_deposit_fees: Opening generally free; minimum balance may apply; non-resident fees not published.
banks: Tatra banka, Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB and ČSOB open accounts for foreigners in branch; app opening requires Slovak/EU residence.
restrictions: No legal ban on non-resident accounts (EUR and FX allowed), but banks set their own residence rules; EU AML and CRS/FATCA reporting.
alternatives: Wise and Revolut provide EUR IBANs usable for SEPA payments.

documents: Passport, Moldovan fiscal code from the State Tax Service (obtained first), proof of foreign address, source-of-funds information; a representative with power of attorney may act.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: maib, Moldindconbank, Victoriabank, OTP Bank Moldova, ProCredit Bank (stricter).
restrictions: Law 62/2008 lets non-residents open accounts without restriction, but Law 308/2017 AML means enhanced due diligence for non-residents; CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise and Revolut for transfers; local e-wallets require Moldovan ID.

documents: Passport, proof of overseas address, proof of income or wealth, tax residency/TIN declaration; certified copies for remote opening.
min_deposit_fees: High thresholds: e.g. Lloyds International £50,000 income or £25,000 savings; HSBC Expat from £50,000 balances or £100,000 salary; Barclays International £40/month if balance under £25,000.
banks: HSBC Expat, Lloyds Bank International, Barclays International (Jersey/Isle of Man offshore arms); onshore high-street banks require a UK address.
restrictions: Standard UK current accounts need a UK address; offshore arms covered by Jersey/IoM deposit schemes not FSCS; strict AML and CRS/FATCA reporting.
alternatives: Wise and Revolut provide GBP account details to Australian residents; some EMIs offer UK sort codes.

documents: Passport, NIE plus certificado de no residente (single procedure since May 2025, via police or consulate), proof of home address, proof of income/source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; non-resident accounts commonly carry monthly maintenance fees.
banks: Santander (non-resident online account with passport reported), Banco Sabadell, CaixaBank, BBVA, Bankinter (cuenta de no residente).
restrictions: Banks must verify non-resident status every two years; Ley 10/2010 AML source-of-funds checks; CRS/FATCA reporting; branch practices vary.
alternatives: Wise and Revolut provide EUR IBANs; Spanish neobanks generally require residence.

documents: Passport plus Iqama for residents; non-residents need either a Visitor ID (from Sept 2025) or written Ministry of Interior/Foreign Affairs approval routed via SAMA.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: Major Saudi banks (e.g. Al Rajhi, SNB) under SAMA rules; visitor-account offerings still emerging.
restrictions: SAMA rule 200.2.3 bars accounts for non-Saudi non-GCC non-residents without ministry approval; visitor accounts reportedly limited in scope; strict AML/KYC.
alternatives: Wise transfers to SAR; STC Bank/urpay and other wallets require Iqama or Saudi ID.

documents: Local ID/residence documents and in-branch presence; no non-resident onboarding documented.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: None known for non-residents; Bank of Khartoum, Omdurman National Bank serve locals and diaspora.
restrictions: Ongoing civil war since 2023, collapsed correspondent banking and international de-risking, residual US sanctions on individuals and entities, severe FX shortages.
alternatives: Bank of Khartoum's Bankak app and exchange houses for diaspora; foreigners use home-country accounts and remittance providers.

documents: Passport, residence permit or long-stay visa, local address proof, proof of income, two photos; enhanced source-of-funds above about DJF 1 million.
min_deposit_fees: Minimum opening deposit required; amounts not published.
banks: BCIMR (BRED group), International Investment Bank (IIB, reported remote opening for non-residents with strict KYC).
restrictions: DJF pegged to USD with free convertibility; AML/CFT rules require in-person verification at most banks; high barriers for non-residents.
alternatives: D-Money and Waafi mobile wallets require local SIM/ID; Wise transfers limited.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, source of funds; PFCA eligibility covers non-nationals visiting or intending to visit Sri Lanka, while Inward Investment Accounts (IIA, ex-SFIDA) cover non-nationals resident abroad.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; varies by bank and currency.
banks: DFCC Bank, Nations Trust Bank, National Savings Bank, Commercial Bank, Sampath Bank, People's Bank.
restrictions: Foreign Exchange Act and CBSL Direction No 04 of 2021 govern permitted credits/debits; IIA funds tied to investment purposes; post-2022 crisis capital-flow controls easing.
alternatives: Wise transfers to LKR; local wallets need Sri Lankan NIC.

documents: Passport or residence card, local address proof, Togolese phone number, sometimes TIN and proof of income, two photos; certified copies by post for diaspora accounts.
min_deposit_fees: Initial deposit required, amount varies by bank and is not published.
banks: Ecobank Togo (Diaspora account, online with couriered originals), Coris Bank International Togo (diaspora account), Orabank Togo (branch).
restrictions: UEMOA/BCEAO exchange regulation (Regulation 06/2024) governs non-resident accounts with heightened documentation since 2025; diaspora products aimed mainly at Togolese abroad.
alternatives: Mobile money (Flooz/Moov, T-Money) requires local SIM; Wise transfers to XOF.

documents: Passport, residence permit or visa, local address proof and income justification; in-branch only.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: None known for non-residents; Ecobank Niger and Bank of Africa Niger serve residents.
restrictions: Military government since 2023 and political isolation, BCEAO Instruction 09/07/2025/RFE tightened non-resident and FX account controls, correspondent-banking de-risking.
alternatives: Mobile money (Airtel Money, Moov/Flooz) requires local SIM; foreigners rely on home accounts and remittance services.
